ObjectName.value: Aunt Edith's Banana Bread Recipe

Categories.value: Sliced banana bread|Flickr images uploaded by Flickr upload bot|Walnut bread

ImageDescription.value:
Aunt Edith's Banana Bread Stays moist a week

1/2 cup shortening or butter 1 cup white sugar 2 eggs 2 very ripe bananas 1 tsp. baking soda 1/2 tsp. salt 2 cups flour (no more) 1 cup chopped walnuts

Cream together shortening and sugar. Add eggs and mix well. Mash in bananas. Combine flour, baking soda and salt (cut back or eliminate salt if using salted butter instead of shortening) and mix into wet ingredients. Stir in walnuts. Bake in a well-greased loaf pan at 350 degrees Fahrenheit for 60-70 minutes or until top is very brown and any cracks in the top are fairly dry inside.

The original recipe had you prepare the loaf pan by greasing it, lining it with waxed paper and greasing the waxed paper. Then when the loaf was done, you removed it from the pan and peeled off the paper. At some point I just stopped doing that and began to grease the pan directly and the results have been fine. I don't really know why that seemed like a necessary step back in the day, but I merely mention it as a curiosity.

ImageDescription.value:
Banana fritters is a dish local to Kerala, they are called by different names in various parts of the state, for example, pazham pozhi, ethaka appam, etc., These are made from ripe bananas.  A dough is made by mixing maida, water, sugar, a pinch of salt, and some cumin seeds. Then the bananas are peeled, cut into either thin long pieces or much smaller pieces, and then mixed with the dough. The bananas are then put into a frying pan filled with oil one by one. Wait till the bananas turn a light golden brown in color. They are crispy on the outside and soft on the inside.
These banana fritters can be eaten alone or you can use a drink to wash it all down.

Credit.value: Own work

The salad was made up out of a failed egg that went thru the egg mould, lol. What's in it?Flying fish roe, egg, nori and butter...will repost when the guinea pig's (my sister :p) verdict on it is up :)

And I don't think the soba noodles were really soba noodles...they said buckwheat noodles on the packet, but did not cook or taste like soba AT ALL.....so I guess there is a difference between both? I got the recipe for how to cook them at justhungry.com >.<

Kamoboko= japanese fish cake
